title: Kissed Gooey Japanese Pork Shio Ramen
description: A jammy, gooey, post-workout Japanese dish featuring black treacle and caramelized pork, this diabetic-friendly Kyushu-style ramen is a hearty and satisfying meal. It is made with shio ramen, a type of Japanese noodle soup that is flavored with salt.
instructions: In a large pot, heat the chicken broth over medium heat until it starts to simmer.
Add the sliced pork belly to the pot and cook until it is browned and caramelized, about 5 minutes.
Add the black treacle, soy sauce, and sesame oil to the pot and stir to combine.
Add the shio ramen noodles to the pot and cook until they are tender, about 3 minutes.
Stir in the sliced green onions and pickled ginger.
Ladle the ramen into bowls and serve immediately.
Garnish with additional green onions and pickled ginger, if desired.
Serve with a side of steamed vegetables, if desired.
Ensure poultry is cooked to an internal temperature of 74°C / 165°F (juices run clear, no pink remaining) before serving.
Note: this recipe is for refrigerator pickling/preserving only — store in the refrigerator and consume within 1 week. Do not water-bath can without an acid (vinegar or lemon juice).
